inputs.prompt:
<Picture 1> is the authoritative spatial map of the world, not a visual-style reference. Treat it as a top-down geometric specification that must be converted into a street-level 3D world. Do not imitate the visual appearance of the map. Infer plausible 3D buildings, roads and vegetation while preserving the 2D spatial relationships: road topology, intersections, building blocks, open areas, water boundaries, vegetation zones, and which side of the route each object is on.

The red polyline is the camera route. Start exactly at the yellow start dot and travel along the red route in its marked direction at cycling speed. Where the route turns, execute the corresponding turn in the world. Do not invent shortcuts, do not cross through buildings, do not leave the mapped road. Buildings and open regions must stay on the same relative side of the route as on the map; water appears only where the map shows water.

Generation task: a continuous, photorealistic first-person bicycle journey through the world specified by <Picture 1>. Camera height about 1.6 meters, smooth forward motion, natural head stabilization, realistic parallax, no cuts, no drone shots, no viewpoint changes.

Visual quality: realistic urban environment, physically plausible scale, realistic architecture, materials and daylight, detailed road surface, sidewalks, trees and facades, coherent perspective.

Hard constraints: the map controls geometry and spatial arrangement; the route controls camera motion. Do not show the map itself inside the generated environment. Do not move roads, buildings or water to make the shot prettier. Prioritize consistency with the map over cinematic composition.
